Trustworthy Data- and ML-Ops for
Intelligent Transportation Systems and Logistics
Antonio Emanuele Cin `aMember, IEEE, Giovanni ScodellerMember, IEEE,
Cecilia Caterina PasqualeMember, IEEE, Silvia SiriSenior, IEEE,
Davide AnguitaSenior, IEEE, Fabio RoliFellow, IEEE,
Simona SaconeSenior, IEEE, Luca OnetoSenior, IEEE
Abstract—The rapid evolution of Intelligent Transportation
Systems and Logistics (ITS&L) has become a cornerstone of
the modern social economy, relying heavily on the integration
of Data, Artificial Intelligence (AI), and, more specifically, Ma-
chine Learning (ML). This paper provides a comprehensive
review of Trustworthy Data and Machine Learning Operations
(DataOpsandMLOps) in the ITS&L domain, underscoring their
importance in improving efficiency, reliability, and decision-
making precision within transportation and logistics services.
We begin by identifying gaps in current literature, offering
clear context for our contribution. Subsequently, we explore the
complexities ofDataOpsandMLOps, discussing their necessity,
key components, available tools, practical insights, and case
studies relevant to ITS&L. Additionally, we address the critical
issue of Trustworthiness in AI applications, examining methods
and tools designed to strengthen confidence in AI systems -
especially in real-world ITS&L scenarios. The paper concludes
with a discussion of persisting challenges and future prospects in
this rapidly advancing field, aiming to serve as a vital resource for
researchers, industry practitioners, and policy makers. Overall,
this work not only establishes a foundational understanding of
DataOpsandMLOpsin ITS&L but also charts a path for further
research and innovation in developing more efficient, sustainable,
and trustworthy intelligent transportation and logistics systems.

portation, Data, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence,

In this survey, we jointly focus on five trustworthiness di-
mensions: robustness, interpretability, fairness, sustainability,
and privacy. We also review tools that support the assessment
of these requirements, helping practitioners evaluate whether
data pipelines, ML models, and deployed services satisfy these

III. INTELLIGENTTRANSPORTATIONSYSTEMS AND
LOGISTICS
In this section, we provide an overview of the main areas
of ITS&L, drawing on several notable reviews in the field [1],
[10], [13], [60], [74], [75]. This overview aims to frame
the problems and opportunities related to Trustworthy Data-
and ML-Ops, which are examined in detail in the following
sections. Building on these existing works, we organize ITS&L
applications into an operational taxonomy tailored to the scope
of this survey. The objective is to group applications that face
similar challenges in terms ofDataOps,MLOps, andTAI,
rather than to provide a purely descriptive classification of
the domain. These applications share common needs, such
as handling large and heterogeneous data, managing task
complexity, and ensuring service trustworthiness. However,
each area also presents specific operational requirements, for
example in terms of real-time processing, scalability, safety,
privacy, fairness, sustainability, or explainability. This taxon-
omy is therefore used in the following sections to organize
the discussion of case studies and to connect each application
area with its most relevant requirements.
Vehicle Control Systems.Vehicle control systems involve
vehicle-level technologies designed to improve vehicle
performance and safety through automation and driver
assistance [13]. Examples of these systems are: advanced
driver-assistance systems [76], vehicle-to-vehicle or vehicle-
to-everything [77], self driving cars [78], electronic stability
control [79], and incident management [80]. These systems
are developed and integrated into self-driving cars to
increase efficiency, improve vehicle handling, and support
humans to correct potential errors or improve their usage
experience [78]. Furthermore, if connected together in a
network [77], these systems can communicate with each

Apache Kafka.Apache Kafka [149], [150] is a distributed
streaming platform widely acclaimed as a messaging system
in real-time data processing. It supports the ingestion and
monitoring phases of theDataOpspipeline. Its versatility
and seamless ability to ingest data from diverse sources,
including web applications and databases, is well known
in both industry and research with more than29thousand
stars on GitHub as of January 2025. The design of the data
processing pipeline not only empowers Kafka to maintain
high throughput and low latency while handling substantial
data volumes but also enables smooth integration with a
diverse array of Apache tools for future data processing.
Finally, Kafka offers robust security measures, encompassing
data encryption during transmission, authentication, and
authorization.
Apache Hadoop Distributed File System.Apache Hadoop
Distributed File System (HDFS) [151], [152] is a distributed
file system that stores vast volumes of data across multiple
cluster nodes. It supports the development of the storage
phase of theDataOpspipeline, being the most used storage
tool in data lakehouse [144], [145]. HDFS is a foundational
component within the Apache framework, boasting more
than14thousand stars on GitHub as of January 2025.
The architecture of HDFS is designed to provide high
reliability (through data replication) and scalability (through
the possibility of adding nodes) in storing and maintaining
large-scale data. HDFS natively deals with variety thanks to
its ability to handle unstructured data, which includes tables,
text, audio, video, images, and more.
Apache Spark.Apache Spark [153], [154] is an open-
source framework for scalable in-memory data processing.
With over37thousand stars on GitHub as of January
2025 it has proven to be the golden standard solution for
implementing the processing phase of theDataOpspipeline.
A key feature of Apache Spark is the distributed (i.e., ability
to leverage multiple nodes) in-memory processing capabilities
reducing the number of disk accesses and leading to a
significant acceleration in data processing. Finally, Apache
Spark seamlessly integrates with various programming
languages and cloud platforms, not limited to Apache’s
offerings but extending to third-party tools.
